subject: Reserved commit duration, SKU split and throughput guarantee proposal for NovusAI
messages:
From: Ava Li <ava.li@novusai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.example>
Cc: procurement@novusai.com
Date: 2027-05-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: capacity sizing + reserved commits — NovusAI initial ask

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We finished a quick internal sizing exercise and want to explore reserved commits for Dedicated to support our inference pipelines (main workload: 2K concurrent conversations, 30k short-completions/day, 75% of traffic < 512 tokens).

High-level asks:
- Pricing scenarios for 12 / 24 / 36 month reserved commits (per-month committed GPU-hours).
- Recommended GPU pool sizing for predictable 99th pct latency targets: target 99th < 180ms for single-turn generation at 4k contexts.
- Throughput guarantees (tokens/sec or requests/sec) you can commit to for each term length and any fallback rules (e.g., soft burst, degraded throughput).
- A proposed ramp schedule / start date window — we prefer a phased start (partial capacity in Jul, full by Sep).
- Any packaging options (SKU split between baseline reserved units + burst credits) and how credits exhaust/renew.

We attached our internal traffic profile and a procurement timeline. Can you send an initial commercial proposal this week? We have budget authority and want to review internal finance before next Wed.

Thanks,
Ava
Ava Li
Head of Platform
NovusAI
Attachments: NovusAI_traffic_profile_v1.csv

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.example>
To: Ava Li <ava.li@novusai.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example, mina_haddad@redwood.example
Date: 2027-05-02T16:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: capacity sizing + reserved commits — initial options

Ava — thanks, this is clear and very helpful. Attached are two artifacts: a short PDF with three commercial term scenarios and an .xlsx with SKU estimates by GPU type (both attached). Summary below; full numbers in the PDF.

Executive summary (high level):
- 12-mo: lowest up-front discount, best for teams wanting flexibility. Suggested baseline: 12 x A100-80GB equivalent slots (sized for 2k concurrent with conservative batching).
- 24-mo: meaningful discount (~18–22% off list), recommend staged ramp (40% active first 30 days, 75% by month 3, 100% by month 6). Includes 10% burst credit pool.
- 36-mo: deepest discount (~28–32% off list), suitable if Novus wants price stability and committed throughput SLAs (we can commit to a per-GPU 99th pct target and a cluster-level tokens/sec floor).

Throughput guarantees / fallback: we propose cluster-level SLOs (tokens/sec floor) tied to committed GPUs, with automatic soft-burst policy that allows up to +25% sustained bursts for up to 72 hours per month. True hard guarantees require 24/36-mo terms with minimum pool sizes.

Ramp window: we can start partial capacity as early as 2027-07-15 (provisioning dependent on inventory). Recommended staging: 30% July, 60% Aug, 100% Sep 1. We can accelerate if you confirm SKU preference (A100 vs H100 style profiles).

Next steps:
1) We want to validate the target latency envelope — please confirm expected p99 target as above or share any tighter constraints.
2) If 24/36-mo looks interesting, procurement tends to request an explicit discount matrix and invoice cadence (monthly vs quarterly).
3) I’ll loop in Karthik for a written counter with discount anchors and throughput language.

Thanks — sending the PDF and SKU sheet now.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: NovusAI_Commercial_Term_Scenarios.pdf; NovusAI_SKU_Estimates.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.example>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example, mina_haddad@redwood.example
Date: 2027-05-03T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: pricing anchors & recommended SLA language (internal)

Looping in some proposed commercial language and a pricing anchor matrix — pulling from recent deals but tuned for Novus profile. Key points for negotiation: 

- Term anchors (monthly committed GPU-hours equivalent):
  * 12mo: base discount 8–12% vs list, no hard cluster SLA; we offer best-effort throughput and a 5% monthly burst credit pool.
  * 24mo: base discount 18–22%; include soft SLA: cluster tokens/sec floor = 70% of steady-state expected traffic, with credit remediation if we miss >2 months of SLA. Burst pool 10%.
  * 36mo: base discount 28–32%; hard SLA: cluster tokens/sec floor = 85% and guaranteed p99 latency target (e.g., p99 < 180ms for a stated model class). Burst pool 15%.

- SKU split recommendation: commit to a baseline pool expressed as "GPU-hour-equivalents" (customer-visible SKU units) + separate on-demand/burst credits. This lets procurement show a single committed line item and an explicit burst bucket.

- Ramp schedule (suggested):
  * Phase A (Day 0–30): 30% baseline capacity active for smoke tests and ingest validation.
  * Phase B (Day 31–90): 60–80% active as we harden batching and KV cache warm-up.
  * Phase C (By Day 92–120): 100% active.
  * If Novus needs earlier full activation, we can offer a one-time accelerated provisioning fee or convert more on-demand hours into committed slots at a blended rate.

- Guarantee language: include a remediation credit ladder (5% of monthly invoice for single missed quarter-level SLO, 10% for repeat within same contract year) but cap remediation exposure to a small percentage of annual contract value.

- Commercial ask: propose we start with a 24-mo anchor at 75% of projected baseline (to balance price vs flexibility); leave rights to increase committed units each 12 months with a lookback pricing refresh.

I recommend we present the 24-mo anchor first (best balance) but keep the 36-mo option on the table with the improved SLA language. Vanessa — can you review the attached matrix (sheet "Anchors") and confirm if finance is comfortable with the proposed remediation cap?

-Karthik

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.example>
To: Ava Li <ava.li@novusai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-05-04T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: capacity sizing + reserved commits — Redwood counterproposal (ND-2027-1087)

Ava — appreciate the quick turnaround on your side. Per internal alignment, please find our counterproposal summary below; full term sheet attached (NovusAI_Commercial_Term_Scenarios.pdf).

Counterproposal (high level):
- Anchor term: 24 months (ND-2027-1087), committed baseline = 18 GPU-hour-equivalent slots (A100-equivalent) billed monthly.
- Discount: 20% off list for baseline committed units; 10% discount on any committed increases within first 12 months.
- Ramp: phased provisioning — 30% active within 30 days of signed agreement, 70% active by month 2, full 100% active by month 4 (target full capacity 2027-09-01).
- Burst credits: 10% monthly burst pool included; additional on-demand capacity at blended on-demand rate.
- SLA & remediation: cluster tokens/sec floor = 75% of expected steady-state traffic; p99 latency target = 180ms for the declared model class. Remediation credit ladder: 5% monthly credit for first missed quarter-level SLO, 10% for second within same year (cap 2% of ARR).
- Acceleration option: one-time provisioning fee to move to 100% within 30 days or convert additional on-demand hours into committed slots at a blended rate (we included numbers in the attached Excel).

Docs / next steps:
1) If this aligns, please confirm an intent email and we’ll send a redline-ready term sheet and DocuSign link.
2) Finance note: invoice cadence will default to monthly unless procurement requests quarterly invoicing (we can accommodate).
3) Operations: our onboarding team will require a test window the week prior to first partial activation to validate KV cache warm-up and prefix caching behavior.

Ava — happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow to walk through the sheet. If Novus prefers a 36-mo trade we can push deeper discount and stronger SLA language; I left that option in the PDF.

Thanks,
— Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
